title: Regular Polygons Constructible with Multi-Fold Origami but Not Marked Ruler
description: Proves that multi-fold origami is strictly more powerful than a marked ruler (neusis) by exhibiting specific regular polygons — the 11-gon and 23-gon — that are constructible with 2-fold (respectively 4-fold) origami but not with a marked ruler. The key algebraic criterion: an n-gon requires a marked ruler iff φ(n) divides some 2^a·3^b; having a prime factor > 3 in φ(n) blocks neusis constructibility.

overview:
The constructibility hierarchy from the existing gallery places compass-and-straightedge, marked ruler (= 1-fold origami), and multi-fold origami at progressively more powerful levels. This entry proves the marked-ruler/multi-fold gap is strict by finding concrete witnesses.

The algebraic key: an n-gon is marked-ruler-constructible iff φ(n) | 2^a·3^b for some a, b (IsTwoThreeNumber). It is k-fold origami constructible iff φ(n) is p_{k+1}-smooth (IsKFoldConstructible). Whenever φ(n) has a prime factor q > 3, the n-gon is NOT marked-ruler-constructible but IS k-fold constructible for appropriate k.

**11-gon**: φ(11) = 10 = 2·5. The factor 5 > 3 blocks neusis. But 5 ≤ 5 = p_2, so it IS 2-fold constructible.

**23-gon**: φ(23) = 22 = 2·11. The factor 11 > 3 blocks neusis. But 11 ≤ 11 = p_4, so it IS 4-fold constructible.

openQuestions.question: Which prime n-gons require exactly k-fold origami and no fewer? Characterize the minimal fold level as a function of the prime factorization of φ(n).
Is the conjectured k-fold = p_{k+1}-smooth correspondence provable from the Huzita-Hatori axioms for k ≥ 3? (The k=1,2 cases are known; k ≥ 3 remains open.)

sections.title: General Non-Neusis Criterion
sections.description: The general lemma: if prime q > 3 divides d, then d ∉ IsTwoThreeNumber. Proof by prime divisibility and the impossibility of 5 | 2 or 5 | 3.

sections.title: The Regular 11-Gon
sections.description: φ(11) = 10 = 2·5. The prime factor 5 > 3 blocks neusis. Since 10 = 2·5 is 5-smooth and foldPrimeBound 2 = 5, the 11-gon is 2-fold origami constructible.

sections.title: The Regular 23-Gon
sections.description: φ(23) = 22 = 2·11. The prime factor 11 > 3 blocks neusis. Since 22 = 2·11 is 11-smooth and foldPrimeBound 4 = 11, the 23-gon is 4-fold origami constructible.

sections.title: Main Theorem and Infinite Family
sections.description: multi_fold_strictly_stronger_than_neusis asserts the strict gap; exists_ngon_at_each_level shows that for every fold level k ≥ 2, some n-gon requires that level but not marked ruler.
